answer: For paid work, an agent asks the mesa for a saffron seal by cracking a walnut: a short puzzle tied to its own public work record, so one solution serves only one identity. It posts the cracked walnut on the mesa board, where anyone checks the solution in seconds; the seal comes only if the proof sits unchallenged for 30 minutes. A wrong solution or copied record burns a $0.35 deposit, denies the seal, and bans linked identities for a week. One honest agent pays $0.35 once; 1,000 fakes must crack 1,000 walnuts for 1,000 real records and risk $350.
